# Finding reference

Every finding id the engine can emit: 169 ids (rules_version 2.1.0: 67 privilege-escalation and 10 dangerous-permission rules; the rest are declared by the analyzers and the engine core). An id outside this list is rejected when the finding is recorded (`GraphBuilder.add_finding`).

Each finding in `graph.json` / `findings.json` carries a `reference` URL: `https://github.com/0xj4f/aws-enumerator/blob/v<version>/docs/attack_paths.md#<anchor>`, pinned to the release tag of the version that ran the analysis (this build: `v0.3.0`), never to the `main` branch. The anchor is the **Documentation** section below, a heading of [attack_paths.md](../attack_paths.md); every id also has its own heading there and here (`#<id in lower case>`).

Former ids (accepted as aliases for one release; the canonical id is written): `SECRET-XAUTH-001` → `SECRET-XACCT-001`.

## ACCESSANALYZER-001

- **Title:** No IAM Access Analyzer for external access in this region
- **Severity policy:** up to LOW (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `posture_detection`
- **Description:** No IAM Access Analyzer for external access in this region
- **Remediation:** Create an account (or organization) analyzer for external access in every region.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#methodology](../attack_paths.md#methodology) (section), [ACCESSANALYZER-001](../attack_paths.md#accessanalyzer-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.posture`

## ADMIN-001

- **Title:** Administrator-equivalent principal
- **Severity policy:** up to CRITICAL (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `dangerous_permission`
- **Description:** The principal can perform every action in the account; its individual privilege-escalation and dangerous-permission findings are summarised in this one finding.
- **Remediation:** Treat this principal as an account administrator: limit who can use it (trust policy, group membership, credentials), require MFA, and replace broad grants (Action:\* or iam:\*) by the permissions it needs.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#high-value-targets-to-hunt](../attack_paths.md#high-value-targets-to-hunt) (section), [ADMIN-001](../attack_paths.md#admin-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.rules.subsume`

## AMI-PUB-001

- **Title:** AMI is shared publicly
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `ami_public`
- **Description:** AMI is shared publicly
- **Remediation:** Make the AMI private (remove the 'all' launch permission) and turn on AMI Block Public Access.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#resource-exposure--external-access-findings](../attack_paths.md#resource-exposure--external-access-findings) (section), [AMI-PUB-001](../attack_paths.md#ami-pub-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.ec2`

## AMI-XACCT-001

- **Title:** AMI is shared with another account
- **Severity policy:** up to MEDIUM (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `ami_cross_account`
- **Description:** AMI is shared with another account
- **Remediation:** Verify the cross-account launch permission is intended.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#resource-exposure--external-access-findings](../attack_paths.md#resource-exposure--external-access-findings) (section), [AMI-XACCT-001](../attack_paths.md#ami-xacct-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.ec2`
- **One finding per:** node and target-account (fingerprint discriminator)

## APIGW-AUTH-001

- **Title:** API has Lambda routes without authentication
- **Severity policy:** up to MEDIUM (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `apigw_public`
- **Description:** API has Lambda routes without authentication
- **Remediation:** Attach an authorizer (IAM, Cognito, JWT or Lambda) to the listed routes, or confirm that unauthenticated access is intended.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#resource-exposure--external-access-findings](../attack_paths.md#resource-exposure--external-access-findings) (section), [APIGW-AUTH-001](../attack_paths.md#apigw-auth-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.data_stores`

## CLOUDTRAIL-001

- **Title:** No CloudTrail trail logs this region
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `posture_logging`
- **Description:** No CloudTrail trail logs this region
- **Remediation:** Create a multi-region trail (or an organization trail) that logs management events, with log file validation and a protected destination bucket.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#methodology](../attack_paths.md#methodology) (section), [CLOUDTRAIL-001](../attack_paths.md#cloudtrail-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.posture`

## CLOUDTRAIL-002

- **Title:** CloudTrail trail is not logging
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `posture_logging`
- **Description:** CloudTrail trail is not logging
- **Remediation:** Start logging on the trail (cloudtrail:StartLogging) and alert on StopLogging / DeleteTrail.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#methodology](../attack_paths.md#methodology) (section), [CLOUDTRAIL-002](../attack_paths.md#cloudtrail-002) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.posture`

## CLOUDTRAIL-003

- **Title:** CloudTrail trail logs write management events only
- **Severity policy:** up to MEDIUM (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `posture_logging`
- **Description:** CloudTrail trail logs write management events only
- **Remediation:** Log read and write management events (ReadWriteType All) so that reconnaissance is recorded.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#methodology](../attack_paths.md#methodology) (section), [CLOUDTRAIL-003](../attack_paths.md#cloudtrail-003) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.posture`

## CLOUDTRAIL-004

- **Title:** No CloudTrail trail records data events
- **Severity policy:** up to LOW (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `posture_logging`
- **Description:** No CloudTrail trail records data events
- **Remediation:** Add data-event selectors (S3 objects, Lambda invocations) for the sensitive resources.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#methodology](../attack_paths.md#methodology) (section), [CLOUDTRAIL-004](../attack_paths.md#cloudtrail-004) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.posture`

## CODEBUILD-WEBHOOK-001

- **Title:** CodeBuild project builds on repository webhooks
- **Severity policy:** up to MEDIUM (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `compute_pipeline`
- **Description:** CodeBuild project builds on repository webhooks
- **Remediation:** Restrict webhook filter groups (ACTOR\_ACCOUNT\_ID, branch filters, no pull requests from forks), give the service role least privilege and require approval for builds of untrusted contributions.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns](../attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns) (section), [CODEBUILD-WEBHOOK-001](../attack_paths.md#codebuild-webhook-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.compute`

## COGNITO-AUTH-PUBLIC-001

- **Title:** The authenticated role of an identity pool is effectively public
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `cognito_auth_public`
- **Description:** The authenticated role of an identity pool is effectively public
- **Remediation:** Disable self sign-up on the linked user pool (or require admin approval), remove public social providers, or use rules-based role mapping that gives sign-ups an unprivileged role.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-7--cognito-unauthenticated-identity-pool](../attack_paths.md#scenario-7--cognito-unauthenticated-identity-pool) (section), [COGNITO-AUTH-PUBLIC-001](../attack_paths.md#cognito-auth-public-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.cognito`

## COGNITO-CLASSIC-001

- **Title:** Identity pool allows the classic flow
- **Severity policy:** up to MEDIUM (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `cognito_classic_flow`
- **Description:** Identity pool allows the classic flow
- **Remediation:** Set AllowClassicFlow=false and make every role trust policy require the pool id (aud) and the expected amr.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-7--cognito-unauthenticated-identity-pool](../attack_paths.md#scenario-7--cognito-unauthenticated-identity-pool) (section), [COGNITO-CLASSIC-001](../attack_paths.md#cognito-classic-001) (finding)

- **Severity policy:** up to INFO (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `coverage`
- **Description:** Input data could not be collected
- **Remediation:** Grant the read permissions listed in the finding (aws-enumerator permissions) and re-run the affected modules; until then the exposure of the affected resources is unknown, not absent.

## IAM-POLICY-COLLISION-001

- **Title:** Two managed policies share a name
- **Severity policy:** up to INFO (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `iam_data`
- **Description:** Two managed policies share a name
- **Remediation:** No action needed for the analysis (documents are keyed by ARN); review why a customer policy reuses an AWS-managed policy name, which misleads name-based reviews.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#methodology](../attack_paths.md#methodology) (section), [IAM-POLICY-COLLISION-001](../attack_paths.md#iam-policy-collision-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** engine core (`engine/findings/catalog.py`)
- **One finding per:** node and policy-name (fingerprint discriminator)

## IAM-PWPOL-001

- **Title:** Missing or weak IAM password policy
- **Severity policy:** up to MEDIUM (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `iam_hygiene`
- **Description:** Missing or weak IAM password policy
- **Remediation:** Set an account password policy: length &gt;= 14, all character classes, reuse prevention 24.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet](../attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet) (section), [IAM-PWPOL-001](../attack_paths.md#iam-pwpol-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.iam.hygiene`

## IAM-ROOT-KEY-001

- **Title:** The root user has an active access key
- **Severity policy:** up to CRITICAL (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `iam_hygiene`
- **Description:** The root user has an active access key
- **Remediation:** Delete the root access keys; use IAM roles or users with least privilege instead.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet](../attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet) (section), [IAM-ROOT-KEY-001](../attack_paths.md#iam-root-key-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.iam.hygiene`

## IAM-ROOT-MFA-001

- **Title:** The root user has no MFA device
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `iam_hygiene`
- **Description:** The root user has no MFA device
- **Remediation:** Enable a hardware or virtual MFA device on the root user and store the recovery material offline.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet](../attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet) (section), [IAM-ROOT-MFA-001](../attack_paths.md#iam-root-mfa-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.iam.hygiene`

## IAM-STALE-PRINCIPAL-001

- **Title:** A policy names a deleted principal (unique id)
- **Severity policy:** up to INFO (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `iam_data`
- **Description:** A policy names a deleted principal (unique id)
- **Remediation:** Remove the stale principal from the policy; IAM shows deleted principals by their unique id.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet](../attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet) (section), [IAM-STALE-PRINCIPAL-001](../attack_paths.md#iam-stale-principal-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** engine core (`engine/findings/catalog.py`)
- **One finding per:** node and principal (fingerprint discriminator)

## IAM-USER-MFA-001

- **Title:** Console user without MFA
- **Severity policy:** up to MEDIUM (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `iam_hygiene`
- **Description:** Console user without MFA
- **Remediation:** Require MFA for every console user (an MFA device plus a policy denying actions without aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent), or move people to IAM Identity Center.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet](../attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet) (section), [IAM-USER-MFA-001](../attack_paths.md#iam-user-mfa-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.iam.hygiene`

## K8S-AUTH-001

- **Title:** Kubernetes objects of the cluster were not enumerated
- **Severity policy:** up to INFO (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_coverage`
- **Description:** Kubernetes objects of the cluster were not enumerated
- **Remediation:** Give the collecting identity read access to the cluster (an access entry or aws-auth mapping with the read-only RBAC of 'aws-enumerator permissions --k8s'), or use --k8s-auth kubeconfig/token, and re-run.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-AUTH-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-auth-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-CALLER-001

- **Title:** Kubernetes permissions of the collecting identity
- **Severity policy:** up to INFO (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_coverage`
- **Description:** Kubernetes permissions of the collecting identity
- **Remediation:** No action needed; review whether the collecting identity's Kubernetes rights are broader than intended.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-CALLER-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-caller-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-CAP-001

- **Title:** Container adds dangerous Linux capabilities
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_workload`
- **Description:** Container adds dangerous Linux capabilities
- **Remediation:** Drop the added capabilities (SYS\_ADMIN, SYS\_PTRACE, NET\_ADMIN, ALL ...) and run with the default set.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-CAP-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-cap-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-DEFAULT-SA

- **Title:** Workload runs as the default service account
- **Severity policy:** up to MEDIUM (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_workload`
- **Description:** Workload runs as the default service account
- **Remediation:** Create a dedicated ServiceAccount for this workload, or set automountServiceAccountToken: false.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-DEFAULT-SA](../attack_paths.md#k8s-default-sa) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-ESCALATION-001

- **Title:** Container explicitly allows privilege escalation
- **Severity policy:** up to LOW (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_workload`
- **Description:** Container explicitly allows privilege escalation
- **Remediation:** Set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-ESCALATION-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-escalation-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-HOSTIPC-001

- **Title:** Pod shares the host IPC namespace
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_workload`
- **Description:** Pod shares the host IPC namespace
- **Remediation:** Remove hostIPC: true.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-HOSTIPC-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-hostipc-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-HOSTNET-001

- **Title:** Pod uses the host network
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_workload`
- **Description:** Pod uses the host network
- **Remediation:** Remove hostNetwork: true.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-HOSTNET-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-hostnet-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-HOSTPATH-001

- **Title:** Pod mounts a hostPath volume
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_workload`
- **Description:** Pod mounts a hostPath volume
- **Remediation:** Replace hostPath volumes by persistent volumes or projected sources; never mount the container runtime socket, the kubelet directory or the node's root filesystem.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-HOSTPATH-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-hostpath-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-HOSTPID-001

- **Title:** Pod shares the host PID namespace
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_workload`
- **Description:** Pod shares the host PID namespace
- **Remediation:** Remove hostPID: true.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-HOSTPID-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-hostpid-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-IRSA-002

- **Title:** Service account names an IAM role whose trust does not admit it
- **Severity policy:** up to LOW (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_irsa`
- **Description:** Service account names an IAM role whose trust does not admit it
- **Remediation:** Remove the stale eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation or Pod Identity association, or fix the role's trust policy if the workload needs it.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-IRSA-002](../attack_paths.md#k8s-irsa-002) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`
- **One finding per:** node and role-arn (fingerprint discriminator)

## K8S-IRSA-003

- **Title:** Service account names an IAM role whose trust could not be evaluated
- **Severity policy:** up to INFO (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_irsa`
- **Description:** Service account names an IAM role whose trust could not be evaluated
- **Remediation:** Collect the role (or its account) to verify the trust policy.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-IRSA-003](../attack_paths.md#k8s-irsa-003) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`
- **One finding per:** node and role-arn (fingerprint discriminator)

## K8S-IRSA-ADMIN

- **Title:** Service account can assume an admin IAM role
- **Severity policy:** up to CRITICAL (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_irsa`
- **Description:** Service account can assume an admin IAM role
- **Remediation:** Restrict the role to the permissions the workload needs, and scope its trust policy to this service account (exact sub and aud conditions).
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-IRSA-ADMIN](../attack_paths.md#k8s-irsa-admin) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`
- **One finding per:** node and role-arn (fingerprint discriminator)

## K8S-NET-001

- **Title:** Service is an internet-facing load balancer
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_network`
- **Description:** Service is an internet-facing load balancer
- **Remediation:** Use an internal load balancer (service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-scheme: internal) or restrict loadBalancerSourceRanges.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#resource-exposure--external-access-findings](../attack_paths.md#resource-exposure--external-access-findings) (section), [K8S-NET-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-net-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-NET-002

- **Title:** Ingress exposes services without an authentication annotation
- **Severity policy:** up to MEDIUM (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_network`
- **Description:** Ingress exposes services without an authentication annotation
- **Remediation:** Restrict the ingress or add authentication in front of it.

- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-PRIV-001

- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_workload`
- **Description:** Privileged container
- **Remediation:** Remove privileged: true (regular, init and ephemeral containers).

## K8S-RBAC-001

- **Title:** Service account bound to cluster-admin or a wildcard role
- **Severity policy:** up to CRITICAL (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_rbac`
- **Description:** Service account bound to cluster-admin or a wildcard role
- **Remediation:** Use a more restrictive ClusterRole or a namespaced Role.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-RBAC-001](../attack_paths.md#k8s-rbac-001) (finding)

## K8S-RBAC-002

- **Title:** Role allows every verb on every resource
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_rbac`
- **Description:** Role allows every verb on every resource
- **Remediation:** Restrict verbs and resources to least privilege.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-RBAC-002](../attack_paths.md#k8s-rbac-002) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

## K8S-RBAC-003

- **Title:** An all-identities group or user is bound to an admin role
- **Severity policy:** up to CRITICAL (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `k8s_rbac`
- **Description:** An all-identities group or user is bound to an admin role
- **Remediation:** Remove the binding of system:authenticated / system:unauthenticated / system:anonymous / system:serviceaccounts to cluster-admin or wildcard roles.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod](../attack_paths.md#scenario-2--you-compromised-a-kubernetes-pod) (section), [K8S-RBAC-003](../attack_paths.md#k8s-rbac-003) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.k8s`

- **Title:** Key policy grants everyone
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `kms_public`
- **Description:** Key policy grants everyone
- **Remediation:** Scope the Principal or add a restrictive Condition (kms:CallerAccount, aws:PrincipalOrgID).

- **Category:** `kms_cross_account`
- **Description:** Key policy grants another account
- **Remediation:** Verify that cross-account use of the key is intended; remove accounts that should not use it.

## PRIVESC-001

- **Title:** CreatePolicyVersion: can rewrite a customer-managed policy attached to a principal
- **Severity policy:** CRITICAL when the principal changes its own permissions (or a policy attached to it); HIGH for another principal, raised to CRITICAL when the closure shows it can act as that principal; a conditional decision is lowered one level (weak condition) or two (strong), never below INFO
- **Category:** `privilege_escalation`
- **Description:** Can create a new default version of a customer-managed policy with arbitrary permissions

- **Severity policy:** derived from what is gained: CRITICAL for an admin-equivalent target (or one that reaches the account admin), HIGH for a target with crown-jewel access or when any principal of the kind may be the target (uncollected ones included), MEDIUM otherwise; INFO when no passable role qualifies; a conditional decision is lowered one level (weak condition) or two (strong), never below INFO
- **Category:** `privilege_escalation`
- **Description:** Can take over an existing Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter and run code or API calls as the role it runs as (this resource type is not collected: whether one runs as a privileged role is unknown)
- **Remediation:** Restrict the Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter actions to the resources each principal owns; aws-enumerator does not collect Bedrock AgentCore code interpreters, so review which roles they run as
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns](../attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns) (section), [PRIVESC-059](../attack_paths.md#privesc-059) (finding)
- **Declared by:** rule data (`engine/rules/data/privesc.json`)
- **Rule:** Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter session, class `existing-passrole`, base severity `derived`
- **Needs:** `bedrock-agentcore:StartCodeInterpreterSession` on the target; `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeCodeInterpreter` on the target
- **Graph edges:** —
- **pathfinding.cloud paths:** `bedrock-002`
- **CloudTrail events:** `StartCodeInterpreterSession`, `InvokeCodeInterpreter`

## PRIVESC-064

- **Title:** PassRole+instance profile association: can attach a passed role to an instance it can run commands on
- **Severity policy:** derived from what is gained: CRITICAL for an admin-equivalent target (or one that reaches the account admin), HIGH for a target with crown-jewel access or when any principal of the kind may be the target (uncollected ones included), MEDIUM otherwise; INFO when no passable role qualifies; a conditional decision is lowered one level (weak condition) or two (strong), never below INFO
- **Category:** `privilege_escalation`
- **Description:** Can associate a privileged role's instance profile with an existing instance and run commands there (Systems Manager or EC2 Instance Connect), then use the role's credentials from the instance metadata service
- **Remediation:** Restrict iam:PassRole to specific roles with iam:PassedToService ec2.amazonaws.com, and restrict ec2:AssociateIamInstanceProfile / ReplaceIamInstanceProfileAssociation
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns](../attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns) (section), [PRIVESC-064](../attack_paths.md#privesc-064) (finding)
- **Declared by:** rule data (`engine/rules/data/privesc.json`)
- **Rule:** PassRole+instance profile association, class `new-passrole`, base severity `derived`
- **Needs:** `iam:PassRole` on the target with `iam:PassedToService` = `ec2.amazonaws.com`; one of (`ec2:AssociateIamInstanceProfile`, `ec2:ReplaceIamInstanceProfileAssociation`); one of (`ssm:StartSession`, `ssm:SendCommand`, `ec2-instance-connect:SendSSHPublicKey`)
- **Graph edges:** `CAN_PASS_ROLE_TO` (via ec2)
- **CloudTrail events:** `AssociateIamInstanceProfile`, `ReplaceIamInstanceProfileAssociation`, `StartSession`, `SendCommand`

## PRIVESC-065

- **Title:** PassRole+Auto Scaling: can run code as a passed role on instances an Auto Scaling group launches
- **Severity policy:** derived from what is gained: CRITICAL for an admin-equivalent target (or one that reaches the account admin), HIGH for a target with crown-jewel access or when any principal of the kind may be the target (uncollected ones included), MEDIUM otherwise; INFO when no passable role qualifies; a conditional decision is lowered one level (weak condition) or two (strong), never below INFO
- **Category:** `privilege_escalation`
- **Description:** Can create a launch configuration or launch template with a privileged instance profile and user data, and an Auto Scaling group that launches it
- **Remediation:** Restrict iam:PassRole to specific roles with iam:PassedToService ec2.amazonaws.com, and restrict who can create launch configurations, launch templates and Auto Scaling groups
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns](../attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns) (section), [PRIVESC-065](../attack_paths.md#privesc-065) (finding)
- **Declared by:** rule data (`engine/rules/data/privesc.json`)
- **Rule:** PassRole+Auto Scaling, class `new-passrole`, base severity `derived`
- **Needs:** `iam:PassRole` on the target with `iam:PassedToService` = `ec2.amazonaws.com`; one of (`autoscaling:CreateLaunchConfiguration`, `ec2:CreateLaunchTemplate`); one of (`autoscaling:CreateAutoScalingGroup`, `autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup`)
- **Graph edges:** `CAN_PASS_ROLE_TO` (via ec2)
- **CloudTrail events:** `CreateLaunchConfiguration`, `CreateLaunchTemplate`, `CreateAutoScalingGroup`, `UpdateAutoScalingGroup`

## PRIVESC-066

- **Title:** User permissions boundary removal: can delete or replace the permissions boundary of a user
- **Severity policy:** CRITICAL when the principal changes its own permissions (or a policy attached to it); HIGH for another principal, raised to CRITICAL when the closure shows it can act as that principal; a conditional decision is lowered one level (weak condition) or two (strong), never below INFO
- **Category:** `privilege_escalation`
- **Description:** Can delete or replace the permissions boundary of a user that has one, lifting the cap on its identity policies
- **Remediation:** Deny iam:DeleteUserPermissionsBoundary and iam:PutUserPermissionsBoundary to the principals the boundary is meant to cap (a boundary-protection statement in the boundary itself)
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns](../attack_paths.md#common-privilege-escalation-patterns) (section), [PRIVESC-066](../attack_paths.md#privesc-066) (finding)
- **Declared by:** rule data (`engine/rules/data/privesc.json`)
- **Rule:** User permissions boundary removal, class `principal-modification`, base severity `CRITICAL`
- **Needs:** one of (`iam:DeleteUserPermissionsBoundary` on the target, `iam:PutUserPermissionsBoundary` on the target)
- **Graph edges:** `CAN_ESCALATE`, `CAN_MODIFY_PERMISSIONS_OF`
- **CloudTrail events:** `DeleteUserPermissionsBoundary`, `PutUserPermissionsBoundary`

## S3-PUBLIC-001

- **Title:** Bucket is public through its bucket policy
- **Severity policy:** up to CRITICAL (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `s3_public_access`
- **Description:** Bucket is public through its bucket policy
- **Remediation:** Remove the wildcard Principal or scope it with a principal-restricting condition (aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:SourceVpce, aws:SourceArn); keep Block Public Access (RestrictPublicBuckets) on at account level.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-5--you-have-access-to-an-s3-bucket](../attack_paths.md#scenario-5--you-have-access-to-an-s3-bucket) (section), [S3-PUBLIC-001](../attack_paths.md#s3-public-001) (finding)

## S3-PUBLIC-002

- **Title:** Bucket ACL grants everyone
- **Severity policy:** up to CRITICAL (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `s3_public_access`
- **Description:** Bucket ACL grants everyone
- **Remediation:** Remove the AllUsers / AuthenticatedUsers ACL grants, set Object Ownership to BucketOwnerEnforced (ACLs disabled) and turn on IgnorePublicAcls.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-5--you-have-access-to-an-s3-bucket](../attack_paths.md#scenario-5--you-have-access-to-an-s3-bucket) (section), [S3-PUBLIC-002](../attack_paths.md#s3-public-002) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.analyzers.s3`

## TRUST-001

- **Title:** Role trusts any AWS principal (Principal: \*)
- **Severity policy:** up to CRITICAL (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `trust_policy`
- **Description:** Role trusts any AWS principal (Principal: \*)
- **Remediation:** Restrict Principal to specific accounts or role ARNs; conditions on Principal: \* are only as strong as their weakest key.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet](../attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet) (section), [TRUST-001](../attack_paths.md#trust-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.iam.trust`

## TRUST-002

- **Title:** Role trusts another AWS account
- **Severity policy:** up to HIGH (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `trust_policy`
- **Description:** Role trusts another AWS account
- **Remediation:** Verify the cross-account trust is intended; restrict it to specific role ARNs and require sts:ExternalId (third parties) or aws:PrincipalOrgID (your organisation).
- **Remediation (external-id):** The trust requires sts:ExternalId; keep the value secret per customer and restrict the principal to the vendor's specific role ARN.
- **Remediation (none):** Verify the cross-account trust is intended; restrict it to specific role ARNs and require sts:ExternalId (third parties) or aws:PrincipalOrgID (your organisation).
- **Remediation (org):** The trust is limited to your organisation (aws:PrincipalOrgID / OrgPaths); confirm the organisation boundary is intended.
- **Remediation (other):** Review the trust conditions; prefer sts:ExternalId or aws:PrincipalOrgID guards.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet](../attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet) (section), [TRUST-002](../attack_paths.md#trust-002) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.iam.trust`
- **One finding per:** node and trusted-principal (fingerprint discriminator)

## TRUST-OIDC-001

- **Title:** Role trusts a web identity provider with weak subject or audience conditions
- **Severity policy:** up to CRITICAL (the catalogue severity is the highest; the analyzer may emit it lower, e.g. when conditional)
- **Category:** `trust_policy`
- **Description:** Role trusts a web identity provider with weak subject or audience conditions
- **Remediation:** Require the provider's audience (&lt;host&gt;:aud) and an exact subject (&lt;host&gt;:sub), e.g. repo:&lt;org&gt;/&lt;repo&gt;:ref:refs/heads/main for GitHub or system:serviceaccount:&lt;ns&gt;:&lt;sa&gt; for EKS.
- **Documentation:** [attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet](../attack_paths.md#scenario-6--youre-external-no-foothold-yet) (section), [TRUST-OIDC-001](../attack_paths.md#trust-oidc-001) (finding)
- **Declared by:** `engine.iam.trust`
- **One finding per:** node and principal (fingerprint discriminator)
